thread:
Zoe Park: Heads up — p99 spikes in eu-west-1 starting ~08:12 UTC, p99 ~1.2s (was ~280ms). Queue depth up, admission control firing but tail isn't coming down. Anyone on call?
infra-bot: ALERT: metric=p99_latency region=eu-west-1 value=1200ms window=3m admit_rate=0.82 gpu_util=92%
Mateo Rivera: seeing same. tcp retransmits up between eu1-edge -> eu1-ns (provider-foo). Packet drops ~0.8% on that path.
Priya Shah: also noticing traffic mix shift — new pilot generating many small-step chat requests (seq len ~40) which reduces batching efficiency.
Liang Chen: quick options: 1) increase admission shed to 0.65 (drop more) 2) add 4 prewarm GPUs for 30m 3) route some traffic to dedicated pool in eu2. Cost delta calc: current throughput ~1,200 req/s. Estimate: +4 gpus * 1 GPU-hour = 4 GPU-hours/hr = ~$3.6/hr (on committed pricing) vs shedding 20% reduces unit cost but increases errors. If we want p99 < 500ms we need ~6 extra GPUs by Amdahl-ish queuing sim.
Zoe Park: can we do a blended approach? small immediate admission bump + 2 prewarms while infra remediates peering. Also toggle fallback to quantized v1b for >1s requests.
Mateo Rivera: applied tentative admit-curve tweak (canary 10%):
```
admit_curve:
  base: 0.9
  soft_shed_threshold: 1200  # queue depth
  formula: "admit = max(0.65, 1 - (queue_depth / 2000))"
  smoothing_window: 60s
```
Mateo Rivera: also bumped prefix cache timeout to reduce backend hits for repeat prompts.
Priya Shah: opening ticket with provider-foo NOC (BGP flaps) and cc'ing network team. ETA for initial response ~25m.
Liang Chen: monitoring math quick-check: if we shed to admit=0.75, effective req/s -> 900. With current batching efficiency that cuts backend token QPS such that p99 modeled ~520ms. Adding 2 prewarms drops p99 to ~420ms.
Zoe Park: ok deploy looks good. keep canary 10% for 5m then 50% then full. Watch p99 and error-rate.
Priya Shah: NOC replied — transient peering flap on provider-foo, fix in progress.
infra-bot: UPDATE: metric=p99_latency region=eu-west-1 value=420ms window=5m admit_rate=0.78 gpu_util=86% prewarm_gpus=2
Zoe Park: :thumbsup: seems stable, leaving admit curve in soft mode and extending prewarm for another 30m. I'll log postmortem notes.
Mateo Rivera: will roll back admit smoothing after network fully healed to regain throughput.
infra-bot: RESOLVED: incident closed at 08:32 UTC. Root cause: transient peering packet loss causing batching collapse + traffic mix change. Remediation: admit curve tweak + 2 prewarm GPUs + provider fix.
